answer: Each epoch the network publishes a checkpoint word, called a knoll, and every new identity must answer a signal only a human can produce quickly: a fresh sonnet of fourteen coherent lines built around that word. Peers check each poem against all earlier submissions, so a copied or machine-assembled verse is flagged within one epoch, and each submission carries a 60-token bond slashed in full when the sonnet is judged copied. A hundred fakes would then need a hundred original sonnets and 6,000 tokens at risk, about fifteen hours of writing for nothing.
